title: Simulating alternate voting systems
summary: Primer uses simulations to compare voting systems such as first-past-the-post, approval, ranked choice and others. It shows how each system behaves and can be manipulated, with links to further voting theory resources.
why: HN commenters link it to explain why plurality voting produces two-party systems and how ranked-choice voting suffers spoiler effects.

quote.text: There are mathematical reasons for FPTP to result in two party systems. [0] explains it pretty well.
